test.name: A precise source refining a vague conclusion is an improvement, not a contradiction
test.description: Check 2's first gap. The profile records a birth of '1814' in 'Ireland'; the attached Catholic parish baptism (SD-DRIS-A) states 12 March 1814 at Skibbereen, Co. Cork. Nothing here disagrees -- the precise date falls inside the vague year and the precise parish inside the vague country -- so the source refines the conclusion rather than contradicting it, and reporting it as a finding is noise in a list the skill exists to triage. The shipped body covers numeric drift by record type ('a census age or birth year within a couple of years ... is ordinary variance') but says nothing about a difference in PRECISION rather than in value, so it has no rule that separates this from a conflict. The edit supplies one, and makes it checkable rather than a matter of taste: the test is containment, so '1814' against '12 March 1814' is a refinement while '1814' against '12 March 1815' is a finding. This corpus deliberately also carries a genuine index error (SD-DRIS-B) so that a run which correctly reports no finding for the baptism still has something for the Remediation doctrine, Classification and Signal-versus-noise dimensions to grade -- all three have N/A clauses that would otherwise score null, which is both a weaker test and the shape the review sample's targeted slot pulls in. PRE-EDIT BASELINE (measured 2026-09-07 against the shipped body, scratch run): PASS on every dimension -- and the pass IS the finding. The run classified the civil death registration as 'likely misattributed (worst problem)' and its recommendation read 'Detach this civil registration entry', on a disagreement that is source-vs-source, while stating in the same paragraph that no other tree person could be named as the record's true subject. The judge scored Correctness 3 and Remediation doctrine 3; the detach guard stayed silent correctly, since index_error_source scopes to the Drouin marriage register. Nothing in the suite caught a detach recommended on a conflict. That run is why this test gained the death-pair note below and why rubric.md's Remediation doctrine bars were sharpened. FLAPPED partial/pass/partial across the three 2026-09-08 runs on an unchanged body, which is the signature of an under-specified rule rather than jitter. The cause was step 4's ambiguity paragraph relying on (b)'s 'recommend detaching only here' to forbid a detach on the ambiguous case; under uncertainty the model offered a CONDITIONAL detach of the 1851 entry ('if it does not fit the original return') on two of the three runs. Note ut_source_evaluation_k9t, which carries an explicit no-detach note for that entry, passed all three. Fixed by making the prohibition explicit in the body and by adding the note here.

input.user_message: Audit the sources on Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) and list what is actually wrong with them, worst first.

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions to enumerate what is attached, then record_read each source that carries a record ARK

The profile's birth is '1814' / 'Ireland'. The baptism record (SD-DRIS-A) gives '12 March 1814' / 'Skibbereen, Cork, Ireland'. Grade whether the reply distinguishes a difference in precision from a difference in value: the record's date and place are narrower than the profile's and fall inside them, and no value in either contradicts the other.

Presenting that pair among the things wrong with the profile's sources is over-reporting of the kind this skill's own body warns about -- 'a list padded with non-findings is the same failure as a list padded with backend metadata'. Offering the fuller date and parish as an improvement the researcher could adopt is not a finding and should not be penalised as one.

The record also names a father Timothy and a mother Mary who are on no tool response for the profile. That is a completeness gap in the tree, not a defect in the source, and is outside what this skill audits.

The 1851 census entry (SD-DRIS-E) disagrees with the PROFILE on the township alone -- Melbourne against Sherbrooke -- and carries no birth year, no spouse and no household, so nothing in it decides between a place keyed to the wrong jurisdiction and a same-name man in the next township. It is not part of either source-versus-source pair. Detaching must not be recommended for it, conditionally or otherwise: 'detach it if it turns out not to fit' is a detach recommendation made on evidence that has not decided, and detaching is the one recommendation here that cannot be undone. Re-reading the original return first is the recoverable action.

The Drouin Collection marriage register (SD-DRIS-B) indexes 9 June 1845 against the profile's 9 June 1849 -- same day, same month, same bride, same parish. A marriage register states its date rather than estimating an age, so this is the corpus's genuine index error and the remedy is to go back to the original page and correct the index. The collection is 'database with images', so an image does exist here -- unlike an index-only collection, where there is nothing to re-read.

The 1861 census indexes a birth of 1816, two years off the baptism's 1814. Census ages were estimated, so a two-year drift is ordinary variance and not a finding. Saying nothing about it is acceptable.

The findings count must exclude the baptism refinement and the census drift. Repeated internal ids across the record responses (P1, N1, F1, S1 recurring on unrelated records) are FamilySearch storage artifacts and must not appear as numbered findings or carry a recommended action.
The headstone photograph (SD-DRIS-F) has no record ARK and must be reported as unchecked rather than clean

The burial register (SD-DRIS-C) and the civil death registration (SD-DRIS-D) disagree with EACH OTHER, not with the profile, which records no death date at all. Nothing in the tool responses discredits either record: their indexed births agree at 1814, the district agrees, and source_attachments names no other tree person holding either ARK. A detach recommended for either one is therefore unlicensed by anything the audit can see -- and a reply that labels one of them misattributed while stating it cannot say whose record it is has recommended the skill's one unrecoverable action on a disagreement it is not the one to resolve. Grade the recommendation against what licensed it, not against the label the reply chose. Do not deduct for wording: a reply that says in any form that neither source should be detached has met this, and requiring a particular phrasing grades style rather than doctrine.
